definition.meaning: Equivalent full-game quality performance: recorded rating plus log odds of the observed quality exceeding comparable public full-game player-sides, in 400/ln(10) rating units.
definition.reference: Public complete training games with at least ten nonforced decisions; Gaussian recorded-rating kernels. Game length does not change the reference quality distribution.
definition.selection: Rating bandwidth [200,400,800] selected by five game-disjoint training-fold CRPS; each game has unit total weight.
definition.interpretation: An extrapolation of observed quality to a full-game standard, distinct from length-matched game performance and moves-only ability estimation.
definition.shortGames: With 1..9 nonforced decisions the point is explicitly marked as a short excerpt extrapolation. Zero decisions or fewer than twenty effective peer sides retain recorded rating.
definition.limitations: Not an official rating update, validated ability interval, or evidence that a short game established the displayed strength. Pool/time-control transfer is unvalidated.

context.interpretation: Conditional full-game quality distribution; this assessment does not validate the short-excerpt extrapolation or true rating.

limitations: Recorded Lichess blitz rating prediction, not established ability or Chess.com Elo. Player-disjoint fitting/development splits; validation previously exposed to other studies. No fresh confirmation.
